name: Nivolumab + Ipilimumab (CheckMate-743) for malignant pleural mesothelioma

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Not biomarker-gated. Dual checkpoint blockade (nivolumab anti-PD-1 + ipilimumab anti-CTLA-4) is a first-line option for unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma regardless of PD-L1 status; the greatest survival benefit was in nonepithelioid (biphasic/sarcomatoid) histology. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma v3.2026, and DeVita 12th ed. (CheckMate 743).

histology: malignant pleural mesothelioma (epithelioid, biphasic, or sarcomatoid; largest benefit in biphasic/sarcomatoid histology)
supportiveCare: 6-week (42-day) cycle: nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (or 360 mg flat every 3 weeks) plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks. CheckMate 743 treated up to 2 years; exact stopping rule (2-year cap) is not printed in the provided corpus and should be confirmed clinically. Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 33121 to 33124, 292972.
Monitor for immune-related adverse events from dual checkpoint blockade (higher irAE rate than single-agent): thyroid/endocrine, hepatic, pneumonitis, colitis, dermatologic, hypophysitis.
Nivolumab and hyaluronidase-nvhy subcutaneous injection is NOT approved for concurrent use with IV ipilimumab (guideline footnote f, line 810).
monitoring: immune-related adverse event surveillance (thyroid/endocrine, liver, pneumonitis, colitis, skin, hypophysitis)

doseModificationRules.text: Hold the checkpoint inhibitor(s) and manage per immunotherapy toxicity guidance (corticosteroids for grade 2 or higher; endocrine replacement as needed); permanently discontinue for severe or recurrent irAEs. Dual blockade carries a higher severe-irAE rate.

drugs.name: Nivolumab
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 33121 to 33124, which state that in mesothelioma or NSCLC nivolumab is given at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks OR 360 mg (flat) every 3 weeks, combined with ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks (CheckMate 743 regimen). Modeled here as nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (days 1, 15, 29 within a 42-day / 6-week cycle). SOURCE-STATED ALTERNATIVE: nivolumab 360 mg flat every 3 weeks (basis flat, days 1 and 22 of the 42-day cycle).

provenance.locator: lines 33121 to 33124 (in mesothelioma or NSCLC, nivolumab 360 mg every 3 weeks or 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks with ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks)

drugs.name: Ipilimumab
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 33121 to 33124. Ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks (day 1 of the 42-day / 6-week cycle), combined with nivolumab, in mesothelioma (CheckMate 743).

provenance.locator: lines 33121 to 33124 (in mesothelioma or NSCLC, ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks with nivolumab)
